questions.q: Why is retrying a failed call immediately, in a tight loop, the worst retry strategy?
options: If the external system is struggling because it's overloaded, a flood of immediate retries makes the overload worse instead of giving it room to recover
ServiceNow's platform blocks any script from making more than one HTTP call per transaction
Immediate retries always return a different error than the original request
Immediate retries are actually the best strategy and should always be preferred
questions.explain: A struggling system needs room to recover — hammering it with immediate retries from every caller compounds the overload.

questions.q: In the exponential backoff loop, what does this line do: `backoffMs = backoffMs * 2;`?
options: Doubles the wait time before the next retry attempt, so delays grow 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s instead of staying fixed
Doubles the number of retries allowed overall
Cancels all further retry attempts immediately
Resets the backoff timer back to zero
questions.explain: Doubling the delay on each failed attempt is what makes the backoff exponential rather than a fixed interval.

questions.q: What does it mean for an operation to be "idempotent"?
options: Running it twice produces the same end result as running it once — no duplicate record, no double-processed transaction
It can only ever be called one single time, ever
It always returns an HTTP 429 status code
It runs faster than a non-idempotent operation
questions.explain: Idempotency is exactly that same-end-result-either-way property, and it's what makes an operation safe to retry.

questions.q: Look at this code: `gr.addQuery('u_external_alert_id', externalId); gr.query(); if (gr.next()) { gr.update(); } else { gr.insert(); }`. What problem does this pattern solve?
options: It prevents a retried "create" from inserting a duplicate record, by updating the existing record when the external ID is already present
It deletes any record that already has that external ID
It permanently disables retries for this external ID going forward
It converts the GlideRecord query into a REST Message call
questions.explain: This is the coalesce-on-external-ID pattern: check for an existing record by its external unique ID before deciding whether to insert or update.

questions.q: What does `gs.sleep(backoffMs)` do in the retry loop example?
options: Pauses server-side script execution for the given number of milliseconds, implementing the wait between retry attempts
Permanently stops the script from running again
Sends an HTTP request to the external system to check its health
Deletes the incident record created by the previous attempt
questions.explain: gs.sleep(ms) is a real server-side API that pauses execution for the specified milliseconds — exactly the wait a backoff loop needs between attempts.
